plan.goal: Size the PLINK binary .bed storage for a GWAS genotype dataset of 16008 samples and 7063788 variants, reporting the total .bed size, the largest-chromosome .bed size, and the number of per-chromosome files.
plan.rationale: The .bed binary format packs 2 bits per sample per variant (4 samples/byte). Total .bed size = n_samples × n_variants / 4 / 1e6 MB. Per-chromosome .bed size uses the same rule applied to the largest chromosome's variant count (1197645). The number of per-chromosome files corresponds to the number of chromosomes in the reference genome; for a standard human GWAS dataset this is 25 (22 autosomes + X + Y + MT), consistent with chr1 carrying ~1.2M variants.
caveats: Per-chromosome file count of 25 assumes a standard human reference (22 autosomes + X + Y + MT); verify the actual chromosome count if the dataset uses a non-human genome or excludes sex chromosomes/mitochondria.
The per-chromosome .bed size is computed for the largest chromosome (1197645 variants); other chromosomes will be proportionally smaller.
